lead.hed: U.S. and Japanese crews are filling runway craters across four bases in Japan
lead.insight: U.S. Pacific Fleet said Saturday that Keen Sword 27 has more than 56,000 personnel from seven countries in Japan, including airfield damage repair at Iruma, Misawa, Marine Corps Air Station Iwakuni, and Kadena. Planner Cmdr. Jonathan Henson said the last Keen Sword kept that work on a tabletop, and this year multinational teams are filling hundreds of craters. At Iwakuni, Lt. j.g. Daysy Cruz-Cordero of Navy Mobile Construction Battalion 5 said Seabees are working the repairs with the Japan Self-Defense Force and U.S. Marines. Henson said the Misawa evolution is set to repair 120 craters over three days, around the clock. The official still shows a Marine with Marine Wing Support Squadron 171 directing a loader at Iwakuni on Oct. 22.

political.hed: Heritage says China, Iran, and Cuba are directing protests inside the United States
political.insight: Wednesday's Heritage commentary says evidence is growing that the governments of China, Iran, and Cuba are financing protests in American streets and directing them. The piece cites a Network Contagion Research Institute report. It is argument from that report. It does not reprint a new indictment.

political.hed: Heritage says France is finding out what the socialist bill costs
political.insight: Wednesday's Heritage commentary on Europe says the pressure on Paris is coming from inside France, not from an occupying army, and that the country is learning what happens when the socialist bill comes due. The piece is argument. It does not cite a new budget vote.

political.hed: Law & Liberty asks whether Frank Meyer's fusionism still charts a course
political.insight: Thursday's Law & Liberty essay asks whether Frank Meyer's fusion of liberty and tradition can still help conservatives chart a course. The piece is argument about the books. It does not reprint a floor vote.

tech.hed: The Army opened a sandbox so vendors can get software scanned in minutes
tech.insight: The Army said Friday it launched Project Gatekeeper, a testing sandbox for commercial software. Acting chief information officer Gabe Chiulli said companies used to navigate ad-hoc routes just to get code evaluated, and that an authority to operate often took six to eight months and required an existing defense contract and a common access card. Gatekeeper puts vendor code in isolated containers, runs automated scans, and is meant to cut that evaluation from months to minutes.

tech.hed: AUKUS officials say work on unmanned undersea craft is on track
tech.insight: USNI News reported Friday from San Diego that AUKUS officials say collaboration on autonomous undersea warfare is on track. The piece opens on the Hadalus-XL unmanned underwater vehicle and quotes Ben Rosenthal, chief technology officer at Composite Energy Technologies, on what the craft is for.

tech.hed: Heritage says parents and teachers still lack guidance on AI in school
tech.insight: Thursday's Heritage commentary says Delaware families and the rest of the country are wrestling with how to handle artificial intelligence in school. It notes that Delaware lawmakers created an AI study committee in 2024, and that parents and teachers still need guidance. The piece is argument. It does not cite a new statute.

culture.hed: Providence sets Pope Leo's Paris Mass against a weekend of French riots
culture.insight: Friday's Providence essay sets Pope Leo's first papal visit to France against a weekend the writer calls a night of terror, after nearly a month of protests. The writer reads both events as spiritual conflict, not a coincidence of the calendar. It does not reprint a police tally.
